page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v5 is an EASv5-series virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance utilizes Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports hardware features such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng scores positioning the instance in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU encryption tests also demonstrate top-tier capabilities, alongside strong PassMark memory scores. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and database operations on PassMark fall within the average range. Large-scale LLM text generation, specifically with a 70B model, exhibits poor performance at 2.31 tokens per second, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU and dedicated AMD EPYC cores, the E48as_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The absence of bundled local disks means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale Premium Storage independently. This configuration is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise application servers, and memory-heavy data processing pipelines.
